title: Square and absolute value of a sign derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$. For every coordinate $i$ and every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, the discrete derivative satisfies $(D_i f(x))^2=|D_i f(x)|$, where $D_i f(x)=\frac{f(x_{i\leftarrow0})-f(x_{i\leftarrow1})}{2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is a coordinate in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ (equivalently, an element of $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$)
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. For a real cube function $h$, write $D_i h(x)=\tfrac12(h(x_{i\leftarrow0})-h(x_{i\leftarrow1}))$, where $x_{i\leftarrow b}$ replaces bit $i$ by $b$. For any $h\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, coordinate $i$, and cube point $x$, $(D_i h(x))^2=|D_i h(x)|$.
